doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Playing Dippermouth the way Oliver played it
summary: Mugsy on first sitting in at the Royal Garden and how Oliver's solos should be played.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I played bass drum at St. Mary's Training School right outside of Chicago. They put you on that bass drum, huh? Then I went to snare drum, and then I was just fooling around with the cornet in school. Wasn't even just practicing in between, and first thing you know I was playing cornet with the band. And then I just stayed right there. Is that the way you first started, at school? Yeah. Was it high school? No, grammar school. Grammar school. Well, where did you sit in with, where was Joe playing when you first sat in? Well, I sat in with Joe was at the Royal Garden. And I played Dipper Mouth. And there's only one way to play Dipper Mouth, and that's the way Joe plays it. And if you don't play those three choruses the way Joe played it, it's just not the Dipper Mouth. That's right. So a lot of cornet players, they play it different. I think it's because they can't play it. That's it. It's like Snaggit. Yeah. Because I've heard Joe play Dipper Mouth, and like Louie's cornet chop series, there's only one way to play that, and that's the way Louie plays it. It's like Carnival of Venice. You play that, just as written. Yeah. It's like the other thing, Joe would play Snaggit. Yeah. The introduction of that West End blues, you know, that was Joe Ollipurs. Oh, I didn't know that. Oh yeah. Joe played that introduction. Really? Yeah. What is that song?

Yeah, I hear all those guys. I heard Joe play that a long time before Louie. The funny thing, you play with a different band, you know them things out of the go, but you play it so wrong with different bands, and then you forget how to play it right.
